races.name: British Stallion Studs 'Carrie Red' EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Angel Sense
runners_data.note: Progressive filly for Marco Botti with solid soft-ground and Goodwood form; sits naturally prominent and is comfortable at this trip, 42 days off is worth noting but Botti has runners returning fresh regularly, and the Good to Soft conditions suit her profile well.
runners_data.comment: Angel Sense won last time out and has run over today's trip, but she ranks ninth of twelve on our figures and a speed rating of 67 makes her difficult to fancy at the weights, even if 42 days between runs need not be a concern.

runners_data.name: Kodi Bear Light
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke in strong 14-day form (12/40); natural hold-up filly stepping up from 5-7f, and critically holds a win over 7f on Good which shows she stays — the strong pace suits her to deliver a late run, and Jack Nicholls (3) is a capable claimer.
runners_data.comment: Kodi Bear Light won last time out and has experience over today's trip, with a 30% strike-rate trainer lending strong support; the worry is that unplaced run two starts back could hint at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Downonmainstreet
runners_data.note: Two consecutive wins for Michael Bell going into this, both on Good ground — the step up to 6½f on Good to Soft is the key query, but she races prominently and could track the pace battle without being involved in it, making her a natural beneficiary if the leaders tire.
runners_data.comment: Downonmainstreet arrives in fine nick, winning her last two starts, though she was third three starts back and a seventh four starts back suggests she can be inconsistent; she has run over today's trip and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround from stall four carrying 120 lb.

runners_data.name: Roosike
runners_data.note: One of the three confirmed pace-setters; her only soft-ground run produced a 14th, and her similar-going record reads 0 wins from 4 — the going is a legitimate concern for her ability to sustain the lead she will almost certainly try to take.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying 119 lb from stall 13, Roosike heads here on the back of an unplaced run, though she does have experience over today's trip and going, and showed decent form a winner two starts back.

runners_data.name: Rollthedicebaby
runners_data.note: Has the form to be competitive — a soft-ground winner and placed — but Richard Hannon's filly is a true prominent-style runner who will find herself shuffled wider and further back than ideal given three confirmed leaders dominate the early stages; her STYLE_FIT discount is real here.
runners_data.comment: Rollthedicebaby ran to win four starts back and finished second five starts back, and our rating of 88 suggests she holds strong claims here returning after 21 days; the main risk is a trainer hitting just 4% in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Leucothea
runners_data.note: The third confirmed front-runner; her soft/good-to-soft record shows one placing from six runs, and she has a tendency to be found in mid-table on similar ground, suggesting she may not sustain the lead role she takes.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Leucothea is hard to fancy despite the distance experience and fresh enough return after 19 days, with her trainer's current 4% strike rate a further concern.

runners_data.name: Wondervision
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in her latest run and clearly progressive for Jack Channon, but she is a natural prominent type who will be squeezed for position by the front trio — her best form has come when getting a handy berth uncontested, and that luxury will not be available here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures despite a win last time out, Wondervision faces a stiff ask against a deeper field here, though she has run over today's trip and comes in fresh enough at 24 days between runs.

runners_data.name: Angel In My Heart
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's filly won on Good and placed on Soft, showing versatility, but like Wondervision she is a genuine forwardly-placed runner who will be racing out of her preferred position today — her 2nd at 7f on Soft shows she handles conditions, and she could stay on if she gets clear late.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and a winner two starts back, Angel In My Heart brings some solid recent form to the table, though her speed rating of 65 and draw from stall 10 leave questions, even if she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Bayside
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's hold-up filly holds a win on Soft over 5f and a place over 7f on Soft — she is a natural race-shape beneficiary here, sitting in behind the fast pace, and Cam Hardie has ridden her before; the 32-day absence is no concern given Millman's record with fresh runners.

runners_data.name: Sexy Chick
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner in the field at OR 93 and carries 135lbs — Oisin Murphy adds significant jockey quality, but she has no wins on Soft from one run and her weight burden is substantial in a stamina test on this ground; she races prominently but must overcome a class disadvantage at the weights.
runners_data.comment: Sexy Chick showed plenty when winning three starts back, and with experience over today's trip and going, she arrives on a sound preparation of 21 days, our rating of 99 marking her out as the one to beat off 93 here.

runners_data.name: Art Of Life
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan's Clive Cox filly has been placed in her last two and is a confirmed front-runner — she may be the best of the three pace-setters if she can avoid being dominated early, but her form reads 622 and all runs have come on Good, making the softer ground an unknown variable.
runners_data.comment: Art Of Life has been knocking on the door, finishing second in each of her last two starts, but is yet to score in recent starts and a sixth three runs back raises a question about consistency; she has run over today's trip and comes here fresh enough at 27 days since her last outing.

runners_data.name: Bymiddaytomorrow
runners_data.note: Two consecutive wins on Good at 7f for Ed Walker, suggesting genuine stamina — Ashley Lewis (3) has limited big-race experience, but the horse's record on soft (7th, 8th) from two runs is modest and she may need this ground to be no worse than it already is.
runners_data.comment: Bymiddaytomorrow won back-to-back two and three starts back but flopped last time out, and at 124 lb from stall 11 she faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's trip and going before and her rating of 87 suggests some headroom.

runners_data.name: Speed of Sound
runners_data.note: Consistent filly for Richard Spencer with Saffie Osborne up — placed on Soft before and has a win on Good, sitting at OR 81 with solid recent form; races prominently and could be squeezed for position in the early stages given the pace bias, but her 3rd on Soft is an encouraging pointer.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out for Speed of Sound, but a winner two starts back and with a run over today's trip and going already under her belt, the 21-day freshener looks ideal — the main reservation is whether she can convert that consistency into a clear edge against the top-rated runner.

races.paceDynamic: Art Of Life, Roosike, and Leucothea are three confirmed front-runners set to fight for the lead from the gates, guaranteeing a strong, unrelenting gallop over 6½ furlongs on Good to Soft ground at Doncaster. This contest will be run at a genuine pace from flag to finish, with the lead battle between those three burning energy early and stretching the field, meaning stamina and the ability to sustain effort late will be at a premium. The soft-ish ground compounds this effect, slowing recovery and rewarding horses that travel smoothly through the race rather than those expending energy fighting for position. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and true midfield runners who can settle behind the pace battle, swoop into a fast-finishing position in the straight, and use the strong gallop as a springboard — runners like Kodi Bear Light, Bayside, and Angel Sense are archetypal beneficiaries. The field holds more prominent/front-running types than can all realistically get their favoured position: Rollthedicebaby, Wondervision, and Angel In My Heart are genuine prominent horses who are most likely to find themselves shuffled further back than ideal as the lead trio dictates the early tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way lead battle between Art Of Life, Roosike, and Leucothea burns itself out in the first half of the race, the soft ground amplifying attrition.
scenarios.body: The pace-setters tie each other up, leaving the front three emptying in the final two furlongs as the race degenerates into a stamina test; horses settled in behind by their riders travel with minimum fuss and hit the line strongly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Profits
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up or prominent runners manages to settle just off the hot pace and times a forward move into the straight with cover.
scenarios.body: With the fractions fast but not chaotic, a horse travelling well in fourth or fifth has the ideal slingshot — they avoid the early energy war yet benefit from the strong gallop setting up a true run home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three confirmed leaders — most likely Art Of Life — is allowed to find a comfortable rhythm and the two rivals fade before the damage is done to the leader.
scenarios.body: Art Of Life in particular has shown consistency in placing and, if Roosike and Leucothea fade earlier than they do, a leader who has avoided the worst of the battle could hold on as late runners fail to fully close on soft ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle is so extreme that it creates widespread scrimmaging early, allowing a lower-weighted hold-up type to dart through a gap late at a big price.
scenarios.body: In a race with 13 runners and significant early congestion, a horse with soft-ground form and a clear run late could exploit the resulting disorder cheaply in the market; the soft ground rewards resolution over raw class.

watchPoints.text: Art Of Life, Roosike, and Leucothea will all contest the lead from the start — watch for a fierce three-way pace battle in the opening furlongs that could severely compromise all three before halfway.

Rollthedicebaby, Wondervision, and Angel In My Heart are all natural prominent types who will be forced wider or further back than ideal — watch for significant early crowding and jostling for positions 4-6 as the pace battle pushes them out of their comfort zones.

Roosike's going record on Soft is a red flag — 0 wins and 0 places from 4 similar-ground runs — watch to see whether she is still travelling at halfway or already under pressure, which will tell you how much pace remains in the race.

Kodi Bear Light's yard (K.R. Burke) is firing at 12/40 in the last 14 days — watch for market confidence in the morning as this filly has the profile to be a calculated yard runner in a race whose shape was made for her.

Sexy Chick carries a 14lb penalty at the top of the weights at OR 93 — watch whether Oisin Murphy opts to track the pace from off the pace rather than committing to a prominent position, as her chance depends on not burning energy in the early scramble.

races.name: Weatherbys £300,000 2-Y-O Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Mithaaly
runners_data.note: Consistent placed record of 221 on Good ground and William Buick is a significant booking for a Boughey runner; prominent style means he avoids the very worst of the pace battle while tracking it, and his 6f-7f form suggests the 6½f trip is ideal.
runners_data.comment: Mithaaly arrives on the back of a fine run of form — a winner last time out and placed in both starts before that — but our rating of 79 suggests he may be flattered by his official mark of 86, and 130 lb from stall 11 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Ongombo
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with a hood fitted; his best run was a second on Good over 6f but subsequent Southwell starts were disappointing — needs the pace to collapse dramatically and the form to bounce back.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 14 of 17 on our figures, Ongombo looks hard to fancy, though a runner-up finish last time out and experience over today's trip offer slim encouragement as he lines up from stall 2 carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Satellite Of Love
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good ground but his only soft-ground start produced a fifth, raising a mild going query; he is a genuine front-runner who will fight for the lead and his effort may be wasted in the early speed duel.
runners_data.comment: Won twice in his last three starts but drops below his official mark on our rating, and that gap may count against him in a competitive field; has run over today's trip and going, and 21 days since his last start leaves him reasonably fresh from stall seven carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Stardom Glory
runners_data.note: OR=94 with good placed form at 6f on Good but finished sixth in a 7f Good race last time, and his style means he will be embroiled in the early scramble; trainer Palmer has 2/31 over 14 days suggesting modest current form.
runners_data.comment: Scrambled home a winner two starts back but has disappointed since, finishing sixth last time out; he has run over today's trip and returns after 22 days, though a weight of 130 lb and an official rating of 94 against a rating of 86 suggest he faces a stiff task from stall 3.

runners_data.name: The Dancing Pirate
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy retains the ride on this Balding runner who has form figures of 44273 — consistent without winning; prominent style and Good-ground experience are assets but his headgear note and inability to win from a prominent position are concerns.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, The Dancing Pirate nevertheless brings solid recent form — third last time out and a second three starts back — and has run over today's trip before; 130 lb from stall one is the query.

runners_data.name: Dorigo
runners_data.note: Ran well on soft ground when fourth over 5f at Southwell and has a placed record on Good; his prominent style keeps him out of the very worst of the early dogfight and Kevin Stott is capable in these big-field races, but 0 wins in 4 soft/similar-going starts is a flag.
runners_data.comment: Dorigo shaped with real promise when second two starts back and was only fourth last time out, and with experience over today's trip and going he looks a leading threat at 128 lb from stall four — the main concern is that he remains yet to win in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: A Bear Affair
runners_data.note: The headgear (blinkers) is noted and his soft-ground form shows 1W1P from seven runs in similar conditions, making him one of the better-credentialled hold-up types for this going; Richard Hannon's yard has a modest 14-day strike rate but the horse's style is a natural fit for a pace-collapse scenario.
runners_data.comment: A Bear Affair shaped with real promise when second three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving him an obvious fitness edge at 19 days since last seen; the main concern is a trainer badly out of form, and he remains yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Secret Society
runners_data.note: Two runs on soft ground produced a seventh and a sixth, making the going his primary concern; despite wanting to lead, his form figures lack the class to suggest he can sustain the pace against stronger rivals here.
runners_data.comment: Secret Society has run over today's trip and going before, and a third two starts back offers some encouragement, yet he remains winless in his last three starts and a seventh last time out is harder to ignore — his rating of 80 leaves him mid-pack in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Glory
runners_data.note: Has shown inconsistency with a run of 31040 and finished 11th twice over course-relevant trips; front-running style ensures he adds to the early pressure but his form figures do not suggest he can win from the front against this quality.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Glory won one race in his last five starts and has experience over today's trip, but his two unplaced efforts in recent outings are a concern; 22 days off and carrying 126 lb from stall 13, he looks a midfield proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Night In Vegas
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner in the field at OR=102 with a strong form string (11531) including a soft-ground win, making the going no concern; wants the lead and will be pressed hard by multiple rivals, so the key question is whether he can sustain his effort over 6½f in a pace battle rather than dictating.
runners_data.comment: Night In Vegas arrives in cracking nick, winning last time out and showing three wins in his last five starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, and at 123 lb from stall six, he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Seven Nation Army
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Soft and placed over 6f on Good for Joseph O'Brien; hold-up style from a wide-draw scenario suits a race of this shape perfectly, and David Probert can produce a well-timed challenge when the leaders crack in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Seven Nation Army won two starts back and was runner-up last time out, showing consistent recent form, though his rating of 80 leaves him vulnerable to stronger rivals; he has run over today's trip and returns after 23 days, carrying 120 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Zigazig Ah
runners_data.note: Consistent record of 21152 including wins on Good ground and a recent second; prominent style suits a race where the front-runners overpace, and Saffie Osborne has shown ability to place horses well in competitive 2yo fields.
runners_data.comment: Runners-up last time out and a winner four starts back, Zigazig Ah arrives here on a quick enough turnaround of 19 days and has experience over today's trip, though carrying 118 lb from stall 14 may not make life easy.

runners_data.name: Alfa Hoodini
runners_data.note: One run, a seventh over 7f at Southwell for Ivan Furtado, provides almost no meaningful form guide; the trainer has three runners in this race which may indicate stable confidence, but that single Southwell run over the wrong trip makes assessment very difficult.
runners_data.comment: Alfa Hoodini finished seventh last time out and, ranked last of the field on our figures, is hard to fancy here; a struggling trainer at 1/23 over the last fortnight compounds the concern, though he has run over today's trip and a 14-day break at least brings freshness.

runners_data.name: Backmeifyoucan
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with runs of 8 and 6 at Southwell for Furtado; running style is unknown making pace-map placement speculative, and the Southwell form offers little to work with against rivals with far stronger profiles.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts with finishes of eighth and sixth, Backmeifyoucan faces a stiff task ranked fifteenth of seventeen on our figures, and a trainer striking at just four per cent recently does little to inspire confidence; experience over today's trip is about the best that can be said.

runners_data.name: Blazing Inferno
runners_data.note: A single run, a win over 6f on Good, is the entire form profile; Daniel Tudhope is an excellent jockey appointment and Edward Bethell's yard is in solid form (5/31), but the step into a 17-runner competitive stakes off just one race is a significant unknown.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below the main market rivals at 67, Blazing Inferno is hard to fancy despite winning last time out 14 days ago; he has run over today's trip and carries 130 lb from stall 15, but his slim recent profile makes it difficult to assess his true level.

runners_data.name: God Given Talent
runners_data.note: Trained by William Haggas (13/52 over 14 days, the best strike rate in the race) which is a significant positive angle; prominent style with a win on Good ground but his last three runs show declining form (4, 6, then 19) before a bounce-back fourth, so consistency is the concern.
runners_data.comment: God Given Talent won four starts back and returns on a handy 22-day turnaround having run over today's trip before, giving him a solid claims at 130 lb from stall 17; the worry is that his last three outings have yielded only a fourth at best.

runners_data.name: Icy Moon
runners_data.note: Single run of sixth over 7f at Southwell for Furtado; like stablemates Alfa Hoodini and Backmeifyoucan, the form base is minimal and the unknown running style means this runner is very difficult to place tactically in a 17-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Icy Moon finished sixth last time out and, ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, he makes little appeal here, with a trainer hitting just 4% in recent weeks adding further concern; experience over today's trip and a 14-day turnaround are slim consolations.

races.paceDynamic: Night In Vegas (OR=102, the highest-rated runner), Satellite Of Love, Stardom Glory, Secret Society, and Sovereign Glory all want to lead, ensuring this 6½f contest on Good to Soft ground will be run at a fierce, unrelenting gallop from the outset. With five horses competing for the front, the early sectionals will be brutally quick, and on Doncaster's straight, flat track the pace will not ease — those at the head of affairs will be running on empty well before the finish. The Good to Soft conditions compound the stamina test, draining speed reserves from horses who burn energy scrapping for position in the opening furlong. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit off the pace in midfield or from hold-up positions, conserving energy until the field strings out and the leaders begin to tie up, making Seven Nation Army, A Bear Affair, and Ongombo the stylistic beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If the five-way battle for the lead produces a genuine burn-up that has the front rank wilting from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: The early pace war leaves Night In Vegas, Satellite Of Love, and Stardom Glory floundering in the final furlong as their reserves are depleted by the Good to Soft ground; hold-up and midfield horses surge through the tiring leaders on the wide, flat Doncaster straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Gets A Breather
scenarios.trigger: If Satellite Of Love or Night In Vegas steals a length break early and the others accept positions rather than fight, allowing a controlled front-running display.
scenarios.body: Without a frantic pace war, the leader dictates a strong but manageable tempo, and Good to Soft ground suits a horse with a genuine stamina-laden cruising speed; the field chases but cannot close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace setters cancel each other out and a prominent-travelling horse like Mithaaly or Dorigo threads through from just off the leaders.
scenarios.body: The prominent runners avoid the very worst of the early scrimmage while sitting close enough to capitalise when the true front-runners cry enough; Good to Soft ground rewards the horse with the strongest galloping action rather than pure speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wildcard Unexposed Bolter
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed, lightly raced types — Blazing Inferno or Alfa Hoodini — translates their unknown potential into a performance that bypasses race-fitness concerns.
scenarios.body: Blazing Inferno's sole win came on Good ground over 6f with strong form entitlement, and a strong pace plays into its hands by creating gaps; Alfa Hoodini and Backmeifyoucan are complete unknowns whose Furtado stable has three runners here suggesting a stable confidence play.

watchPoints.text: Night In Vegas and Satellite Of Love are both confirmed front-runners with high ratings — watch the opening two furlongs for a genuine pace duel that could compromise both horses' finishing efforts entirely.

Seven Nation Army won over 7f on Soft for O'Brien and holds hold-up credentials that perfectly suit a pace-collapse scenario — watch for David Probert to be patient and time his challenge when the leaders falter inside the final 2f.

Ivan Furtado runs three lightly raced horses (Alfa Hoodini, Backmeifyoucan, Icy Moon) with minimal form — watch for any market support as a stable-confidence signal given their form is impossible to assess on public evidence alone.

God Given Talent represents William Haggas (best 14-day trainer strike rate in this field at 13/52) but his last three form figures show marked inconsistency — watch whether the market reflects trainer confidence or fades given the patchy recent profile.

With 17 runners on Good to Soft ground over 6½f on a straight track, watch for significant draw and traffic advantages — horses drawn centrally to high are likely to get the clearest run as the pace-setters spread across the track early.

races.name: Pertemps Network Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Runman
runners_data.note: Gosden-trained gelding with two wins this season at 8f on good, stepping up in trip and distance; soft ground is unexplored but a prominent style suits this controlled pace, and Oisin Murphy's booking for a Gosden runner always commands respect — the trip question is the main query.
runners_data.comment: Runman won last time out and has won three times in his last five starts, giving him strong recent claims, and he has run over today's trip and going before; however, ranked fifth of eleven on ratings with a speed figure of 84, he may need to find more to dominate.

runners_data.name: King Of Earth
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 9f for Haggas, including one on soft, and three visits to similar going in last six runs; Tom Marquand rides, the profile is progressive, and the step to 10f looks entirely within reach for a horse still on a career upward curve.
runners_data.comment: King Of Earth won two of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories two and three starts back, and returns fit on 19 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; the concern is that unplaced effort last time out leaves something to prove.

runners_data.name: Knights Charge
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's lightly-raced improver has won twice at 10f including on soft, which is a genuine positive, but 114 days off the track is a significant fitness query; his natural style pushes forward and he will likely be denied that position in this crowded prominent brigade, meaning he races less than ideally.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins boost Knights Charge's claims, though 114 days off the track is a fitness query and he faces stiffer company here; has run over today's trip and going before, and stall one gives him an early position to consider.

runners_data.name: Wild Thoughts
runners_data.note: Four wins from eight and two placed efforts at 8f, but steps up to 10f here and has been below par in last two outings on good ground; genuine front-running instinct will be curtailed with so many pace types present, making it hard for this Spencer runner to produce its best work.
runners_data.comment: Wild Thoughts has shown only two wins in his last six starts, and consecutive finishes of seventh and ninth make the recent second last time out hard to weigh; ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, he is a tough sell, though he has run over today's trip and 26 days off looks a fair prep.

runners_data.name: Bourbon Blues
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Brian Meehan on this hold-up type who has placed at 10f on soft twice from three attempts at similar conditions; class at the top of the weights (135lbs) is a concern but Moore's ability to find a clean late run in a messy field is a key tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second two starts back, Bourbon Blues arrives in fine fettle just 19 days after his most recent outing, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; our rating of 111 marks him out as the one to beat, though he remains yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Spyce
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner for Alan King, who wins only one race per twelve runners at the 14-day level, and Rossa Ryan gets the lead assignment; Spyce has not won since an 8f soft-ground victory and has been beaten in four subsequent starts, but unchallenged control of fractions from the front is a significant positional asset.
runners_data.comment: Spyce has experience over today's trip and conditions, and our rating of 106 marks him as a serious threat in this field, but he was ninth last time out and returns after 82 days off, making fitness the key question.

runners_data.name: Besieged
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's three-run maiden who has placed in all three starts including a soft-ground win at 10f last time; the form is limited but entirely consistent and the soft ground/trip combination aligns perfectly — 93 days off the track and a 4lb claimer-less rider are the cautions.
runners_data.comment: Besieged won last time out and has run over today's trip, but a 93-day absence is a concern, and carrying 127 lb from stall 11 will test his stamina; two seconds in his last three starts suggest he is consistent enough to factor if fit.

runners_data.name: Strength Of Spirit
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's prolific trainer form (12 from 40 over 14 days) is a flag, but this horse's natural desire to race prominently will be frustrated by the volume of similar types; its one win at 9f on good and moderate recent form (8934) suggest it is out of form and out of position.
runners_data.comment: Strength Of Spirit bounced back to winning ways last time out and arrives here race-fit on 30 days' rest, with his trainer firing at a sharp 30% strike rate; he has run over today's trip and going, and 122 lb is the chief query.

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Donny
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's veteran of soft and heavy conditions with two wins at 10f on soft, racing just four days ago which either signals peak fitness or residual fatigue; a genuine hold-up type who handles the drop in the weights well and whose course-form profile (multiple placed efforts at 10f) is directly relevant.
runners_data.comment: Stoneacre Donny won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, yet his record in recent starts also includes a ninth two back, and four days is a quick turnaround; at 121 lb from stall seven, he asks for a leap of faith.

runners_data.name: Sintra
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's runner has won at 10f on good ground but returns after 117 days off, which is the longest absence in the field; naturally inclined to race prominently but the traffic of similar types means she races from midfield instead, and a four-month gap without a racecourse appearance adds significant risk.
runners_data.comment: Sintra has been off the track for 117 days and ranks tenth of eleven on our figures, making him difficult to fancy despite a win two starts back and a record of placing regularly in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Darius Dark
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's hold-up horse is genuine in that role and has three wins at 12f, suggesting stamina is the strength, but dropping to 10f on soft may actually suit the way he stays; moderate recent form (4th last time) and a light winning record at this trip are mild negatives.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Darius Dark has won three times in his last six starts but a fourth and an unplaced effort since, and a speed rating of 73 does little to inspire confidence, though he handles today's going and returns after a 21-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Spyce is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in an 11-runner field over 1m2f on Good To Soft ground, she is likely to coast along at a controlled, energy-conserving tempo rather than being pressed into a gruelling gallop. Runman and King Of Earth will push into prominent positions directly behind, while Bourbon Blues, Stoneacre Donny and Darius Dark will settle in the rear third, eyeing a sustained late run on ground that rewards stamina and finishing kick over raw speed. The field contains considerably more front-running and prominent-minded horses than the shape can accommodate — Knights Charge, Wild Thoughts, Strength Of Spirit and Sintra are all natural prominent types who will be squeezed back into midfield against their instinct, which compromises their effectiveness. A lone, unhurried front-runner on soft ground over this trip historically sets up a race where closers can generate sustained momentum from the home turn, but the key nuance is that the true hold-up horses here (Bourbon Blues, Stoneacre Donny, Darius Dark) are genuine in that role — meaning the race shape most clearly favours the patient, stayer-profile closer who can produce a deep, relentless finish rather than a sharp, speed-based burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Spyce sets a steady, uncontested pace that compresses the field and the genuine hold-up horses produce sustained finishing runs from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Spyce's unhurried fractions on Good To Soft ground mean energy is preserved throughout the field, but the soft surface ensures the race truly tests staying power in the final two furlongs; those who have settled deepest and travel sweetly into the straight are rewarded as the pace collapses late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Control
scenarios.trigger: If Runman or King Of Earth push the tempo noticeably from early, removing the purely steady-pace dynamic and rendering a mid-race surge decisive.
scenarios.body: A more genuinely run race would suit horses who have been prominent throughout and can sustain their effort, particularly at 1m2f where class and rhythm matter; Runman's unbeaten record at this level and King Of Earth's recent back-to-back wins make them the primary beneficiaries of a truly run contest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Spyce is allowed a completely uncontested lead on a shorter-than-expected racing line and the closers are unable to generate sufficient momentum in time.
scenarios.body: On genuinely soft going a front-runner with a clear passage can ration effort and front-run to the line if the pace behind is disorganised; Spyce's solo lead, combined with the redistribution of several prominent types into midfield creating positional chaos, gives her a marginal but real chance of lasting home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Knights Charge, Wild Thoughts, Strength Of Spirit and Sintra into midfield resolves cleanly and one finds a clear run at a crucial moment despite racing out of role.
scenarios.body: This shape depends heavily on horses performing away from their natural position, which materially reduces the probability; however a high-class individual like Knights Charge, who has won twice at this trip and goes well on soft, retains residual claims even from a disadvantaged draw in the shape.

watchPoints.text: Bourbon Blues — Ryan Moore on the highest-rated hold-up horse in the field; if he gets a smooth passage from the home turn on ground the horse handles, his class advantage over rivals with course weight makes him the primary danger regardless of the overall shape.

Spyce's gallop — monitor the opening fractions; if she bowls along completely unchallenged, even moderate tempo on soft ground may prove more taxing than it looks and the closers may not have enough road to reel her in late.

Knights Charge's positioning — 114 days off and forced to race out of his natural prominent role creates a dual fitness and positional hazard; if he emerges wide or is denied a clear run turning in, his chance evaporates despite the strong form profile at this trip and going.

Stoneacre Donny ran only four days ago — watch for any signs of fatigue in the closing stages; if he travels fluently to the two-furlong pole, his soft-ground form at this trip makes him a live threat, but back-to-back runs in quick succession are always worth monitoring on a testing surface.

Redistribution congestion in midfield — with four genuine prominent types (Knights Charge, Wild Thoughts, Strength Of Spirit, Sintra) all pushed back, there is a material risk of traffic problems and interference turning into the straight, which could benefit the wide runners or those drawn widest with clearest passage.

races.name: Betfred Park Hill Fillies' Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Consent
runners_data.note: Proven prominent racer for Prescott with strong soft-ground credentials (1W4P on similar going) and a solid recent run record; drops back from 14f but the 1m6½f trip on Doncaster's flat test suits, and the headgear flag (hg:p) suggests she is kept sharp — 40 days off is well within normal range for this yard.|
runners_data.comment: Consent showed smart form when winning three starts back and filling the runner-up spot on two further occasions in recent starts, and she has distance and going experience to call upon; the worry is her fourth last time out suggests she may need things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Danielle
runners_data.note: Gosden/Buick combination commands attention at this level: two wins from six on soft or similar going make her one of the better ground confirmations in the field, and her style of racing prominently over this sort of trip means she is ideally positioned to benefit from Fairy Glen's controlled lead — 40 days between runs is routine.|
runners_data.comment: Danielle won back-to-back two and three starts back and has experience over today's trip and conditions, with our rating marking her out as the pick of this field; the concern is a below-par sixth last time out after a 40-day absence that now stretches again.

runners_data.name: Fairy Glen
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will set the tempo unchallenged on good-to-soft, but her STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) reflects that she is racing out of her natural role relative to this race shape's dynamics; 112 days off is notable and represents the longest absence in the field — Crisford's yard will need her to come fresh rather than rusty.|
runners_data.comment: Fairy Glen has winning form in recent starts, including a winner two starts back, but she rates well below the field on our figures and returns after 112 days off carrying 133 lb, making her hard to fancy at this level despite her experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Floresta
runners_data.note: Murtagh-trained hold-up type whose form shows she can finish powerfully on soft ground (1W2P on similar), but she has been well beaten in some competitive 14f fields on good ground; the headgear flag (hg:p) is worth noting, and she will need the race to develop at a genuine pace to get competitive from her natural off-the-pace position.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Floresta faces a stiff ask, and 53 days off the track does little to ease concerns, though she has run over today's trip and going before and her last-five record does include two wins.

runners_data.name: Nyra
runners_data.note: Has finished placed consistently at 10-12f on soft and good ground but has not won in recent starts; naturally a prominent racer, she is mapped to midfield here because the field is simply too loaded with pace types — her best chance would come if she can slot closer to the front than her mapped position suggests, though her STYLE_FIT discount (0.90) reflects the difficulty of doing so.|
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, Nyra arrives here as a lively threat — third last time out and a runner-up two starts back, her figures suggest she is better than her official rating of 104, though 54 days off the track and 133 lb to carry are the risks to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Ryka
runners_data.note: The most recent winner in the field (21 days ago, 12f soft), and David O'Meara's horse has genuine form at this level over similar ground; by nature she wants to race prominently, but with Consent, Danielle, and Waardah ahead of her in the queue for those positions, she may be unable to express that style — her STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) is the key caveat.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and her recent form has been patchy — sixth and eighth in her last two starts — though she does boast a win three starts back and has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Waardah
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows' filly boasts three wins from eight runs on soft or similar going, making her one of the standout soft-ground performers here; OR 108 and a headgear flag (hg:h) hint at a horse that needs to be produced with intent — Callum Rodriguez will aim to sit prominent and deliver a sustained challenge through the straight.|
runners_data.comment: Waardah shaped with plenty of encouragement last time, finishing third, and was a runner-up two starts back, showing consistent form around the principals; she has experience over today's trip and going, and 40 days between runs should leave her in good order under 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Cameo
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's mount for Aidan O'Brien is a three-year-old carrying 9lb less than the older fillies, which is a live weight advantage in a staying test; however, her recent form string (515386) is inconsistent and she has not won since taking a 12f handicap, while by nature she wants to race prominently — the field depth means she is mapped to midfield and her STYLE_FIT (0.93) reflects the positional squeeze.|

runners_data.name: Prizeland
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer who won over 12f on soft last time and finished second at 12f on good — her profile is progressive and Oisin Murphy gives her top-level handling; she receives the 3yo weight allowance and is one of the most authentic late-runners in the field, meaning she needs a strong enough pace to deliver her run.|
runners_data.comment: Prizeland won last time out and has winning form in her last five starts, though a fifth three starts back is a minor blemish; she handles today's going and returns after 21 days carrying 124 lb, leaving her with plenty to prove against the top-rated runners here.

races.paceDynamic: Fairy Glen is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press her hard for the lead, she is expected to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-soft ground over 1m6½f — a setup that rewards relaxed, well-positioned horses who travel smoothly without burning energy. Consent, Danielle, and Waardah are the natural prominent players most likely to tuck in directly behind Fairy Glen, giving them a clean view and minimal trouble on the wide, flat Doncaster track. Nyra, Ryka, and Cameo are genuine prominent types by nature but are displaced into midfield here simply because there are more pace-seeking horses than positions available at the front, meaning they will be forced to settle further back than they would prefer. With a single controlled pace-setter and an orderly shape expected, this race tilts clearly toward horses who can travel prominently behind Fairy Glen and sustain their effort through the long straight — front-rank prominent types have a decisive tactical advantage, while true hold-up horses will need a genuine gallop to generate the momentum to close.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fairy Glen Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Fairy Glen leads without serious challenge and the pace remains steady, allowing prominent racers to dictate the finish.
scenarios.body: Fairy Glen sets a sedate tempo into the Doncaster straight, and the horses stationed directly behind her — Consent, Danielle, Waardah — are delivered perfectly poised to quicken in the final two furlongs; with no burst of pace needed early, their fresh legs do the damage late. This strongly suits prominent types with proven soft-ground form and the stamina to sustain, giving the race to those who travel widest into the straight with the clearest passage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Stayer Grinds
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely slow and the race becomes a test of pure stamina in the final furlong rather than a tactical sprint.
scenarios.body: A crawl through the first mile means the final two furlongs turn into a grinding endurance test on tiring good-to-soft ground, rewarding the horse with the most raw staying ability rather than the quickest turn of foot. Floresta and Prizeland, both proven over long distances on soft ground with late-running profiles, could emerge from the pack as the front group flatten out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Make Late Ground
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly strong early gallop is set and the front group ties itself up, allowing hold-up horses to finish through.
scenarios.body: Should Fairy Glen be pressured into a stronger-than-anticipated pace, the hold-up horses Floresta and Prizeland are the genuine beneficiaries — their natural style means they are conserving energy when others are spending it. This scenario is limited in probability because the field's other pace types (Nyra, Ryka, Cameo) have been pushed back through redistribution, not genuine preference, so they will not sustain true hold-up running to deliver a late challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Fairy Glen Sustains to Win
scenarios.trigger: If Fairy Glen's front-running form translates and she steals a decisive break at a solo-set pace, never being headed.
scenarios.body: Racing from the front on familiar soft ground with no genuine rival for the lead, Fairy Glen could exploit her ability to control the fractions and simply outstay the field up the straight if the prominent horses behind her lose the thread or are checked by traffic. Her STYLE_FIT tag reflects she is racing out of her usual role in terms of overall contest dynamics, so this remains the least likely outcome despite her obvious positional advantage.

watchPoints.text: Fairy Glen's 112-day absence is the longest in the field — watch the market for any late drift that suggests she is not fully forward, as her ability to control the pace is the foundation of the dominant scenario.

Ryka and Nyra are both natural prominent racers who cannot all get their position — watch the first two furlongs for signs of positional scrapping or hard-ridden early moves that could compromise their races or inject unexpected pace into what should be a controlled tempo.

Cameo (Ryan Moore) is officially mapped to midfield but Moore's race-reading may see him push forward early to claim a better pitch — if he does, the pace dynamic could shift and the scenario probabilities compress toward the closers.

Prizeland and Floresta are the field's genuine hold-up types; watch whether the pace is truly strong enough through the first mile to allow them to close — if Fairy Glen crawls, their late runs may simply arrive too late on a flat, straight track.

Waardah carries a headgear flag (hh) and has three wins on soft ground — watch how freely she travels in the early stages behind Fairy Glen, as any sign of her being restrained or keen could determine whether she finishes powerfully or flattens out in the closing stages.

races.name: Betfred May Hill Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Ballyskeagh
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Joseph O'Brien who has won over a mile on good ground and shaped with promise in defeat over eight furlongs; the step to soft ground looks fine given breeding, and the extra wait of 12 days keeps freshness; will need the pace war to fully materialise before delivering late.|
runners_data.comment: Ballyskeagh arrives on the back of a second last time out, and a winner two starts back, bringing strong recent form into this assignment; she has run over today's trip and returns after just 12 days, suggesting she remains in good order.

runners_data.name: Beguiled
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden filly who won on debut over seven furlongs in good company and steps up to a mile for the first time; James Doyle takes the ride for a yard firing at 37% over 14 days, and prominent style means she can track the leaders without being caught up in the early front-running contest.|
runners_data.comment: Beguiled won last time out and has run over today's trip, but our rating of 87 ranks her eighth of eleven and the 128 lb burden is no help, leaving her with something to prove against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Eabha
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly has placed twice on soft ground and won twice on good, making her the most proven performer in similar conditions in the field; she travels prominently and has the profile to sit just off the contested pace before asserting, with multiple wins over seven furlongs suggesting the mile is within range.|
runners_data.comment: Eabha arrives here in fine fettle, second last time out and a winner three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour after a sharp 11-day turnaround; the chief concern is that her official rating of 98 leaves her carrying 128 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Martinet
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's front-runner carries a 33-day absence into this step up in class; Luke Morris rides and the yard runs at 28% over 14 days, though Martinet will have to battle three or four rivals for early lead position which on soft ground could cost him dearly in the final stages.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below her official mark on our figures and likely up against stronger rivals rated ahead of her, Martinet does have a win in her last three starts and has run over today's trip, but carrying 128 lb from stall 10 makes this a tough task.

runners_data.name: Musical Times
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two starts for Charlie Appleby, both comfortable wins over seven furlongs on good ground; William Buick takes over and the 70-day break could mean the gelding returns cherry ripe, though this is the first time he faces soft ground and a contested early pace could undermine his preference for controlling proceedings.|
runners_data.comment: Musical Times arrives in fine nick with back-to-back wins in her last two starts, though 70 days off the track raises a fitness query; she has run over today's trip before and carries 128 lb from stall 3, and our rating of 95 suggests she holds her own in this field without dominating it.

runners_data.name: Scommessa Sicura
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy rides for Andrew Balding, who is in strong form at 20% over 14 days; front-running profile but has a pattern of finishing second — five times in recent starts — suggesting rivals consistently find more and the pace battle ahead may expose that tendency again on ground she has faced once before.|
runners_data.comment: Scommessa Sicura arrives in fine nick, a winner two starts back and placed either side of that, with experience of today's trip and going working in her favour; the chief concern is whether stall 11 suits at the break.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Rain
runners_data.note: Jim Bolger's filly arrives as the highest-rated runner in the field at OR 101 and has won over a mile on good ground as recently as 12 days ago; Rossa Ryan rides for a yard that ran one winner from six runners over the fortnight, and her prominent-to-tracking style is ideally suited to sitting just off a contested front-running battle before asserting quality.|
runners_data.comment: Sea Of Rain won last time out and has run over today's trip, carrying a workable 128 lb from stall four with a lively 12-day turnaround; the slight dip from her official mark to our rating of 97 is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Speckles
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien combine, always commanding attention, but Speckles has finished sixth, second, and fifth in her last three starts and her form profile looks a shade below the principals here; prominent style means she won't be far away early, but she will need a significant upgrade to figure at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Speckles nevertheless showed a second two runs back and returns on a quick 12-day turnaround having run over today's trip, though her fifth most recently and a rating of 95 leave her with plenty to prove from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Tall Trees
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's filly broke her maiden over seven furlongs 12 days ago and now steps markedly up in class and trip; Tom Marquand rides and the yard runs at 31% over 14 days, but Tall Trees will be competing for the lead against three seasoned front-runners which is a tough introduction to Group 2 company.|
runners_data.comment: Tall Trees won last time out and has run over today's trip, but her rating of 91 ranks her seventh of eleven here and that speed figure of 83 gives the handicapper little room to flatter; the 128 lb burden from stall two is the weight to watch.

runners_data.name: Thuritha
runners_data.note: David Simcock's hold-up filly won over a mile at Sandown on standard going last time and arrives 14 days fresh; Sean Levey takes the ride and the soft surface is an unknown factor, but the hold-up style is at least suited to the pace dynamics if she can find the necessary class to be competitive at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and eight pounds below her official mark in terms of our assessment, Thuritha's two fifths in recent starts make her hard to fancy despite a win last time out and experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Tie A Navyribbon
runners_data.note: Front-running winner over a mile on good ground for William Stone, whose yard has had just one runner over the past fortnight; Josephine Gordon takes the ride, and while the recent mile win is relevant, Tie A Navyribbon must fight at least three other confirmed front-runners for space and faces a sharp class climb into Group 2 company.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and rated 4 lb below her official mark, Tie A Navyribbon is hard to fancy despite a winner last time out; she has run over today's trip and returns after 21 days, but the ratings profile makes her a tough sell.

races.paceDynamic: Musical Times, Scommessa Sicura, Tall Trees, and Martinet all carry front-running profiles into a one-mile contest on Good To Soft ground at Doncaster, guaranteeing a genuinely contested early gallop with no single horse able to dictate unchallenged. That four-way battle for supremacy across the first two to three furlongs will burn energy in the soft underfoot conditions, compressing the field and ensuring the pace remains honest throughout rather than collapsing into a sprint finish. Doncaster's straight mile on this ground rewards horses who travel smoothly within themselves early and possess the stamina to grind past tiring leaders in the final two furlongs, making the race shape a direct test of resolution at trip. This setup heavily favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can settle just off the contested lead, conserve energy, and pounce when the front-runners tie up — Sea Of Rain and Ballyskeagh profile as the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners fight for position and set a genuinely strong early gallop that burns them out on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Musical Times, Scommessa Sicura, Martinet, and Tall Trees will push each other along from the outset, leaving them vulnerable in the final two furlongs on tiring ground; hold-up and midfield horses who have settled quietly will sprint past fading leaders on the run to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Rails Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner breaks cleanly and establishes a clear lead while rivals check each other in the early scramble.
scenarios.body: The initial contest for the lead may see one horse — most likely Musical Times — slip clear while rivals jostle behind, allowing them to dictate a sustainable rhythm and prove impossible to reel in on soft ground; the Appleby-Buick combination thrives in exactly this controlled front-running scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stamina Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but even, and the race becomes a true stamina test in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: On genuinely soft ground over a mile, the field could compress into a wall of horses three furlongs out with the outcome settled purely by who stays on most powerfully; runners with demonstrated soft-ground form and a mile trip suit profile to outlast rivals who may be found wanting for stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners collectively ease the tempo mid-race and allow a sprint-finish scenario in the straight.
scenarios.body: Soft ground makes this unlikely as it naturally sustains a grinding gallop, but if the pace somehow drops in the middle section it could hand an advantage to a prominent runner who quickens off a slow pace; this scenario most benefits a horse like Speckles who has looked capable of a late turn of foot.

watchPoints.text: Musical Times, Scommessa Sicura, Tall Trees, and Martinet are all drawn to lead — watch for a fierce battle for early supremacy that could burn out every one of them before halfway on soft ground.

Sea Of Rain arrives as the highest-rated runner and is equipped to track the contested pace before unleashing — if the front-runners do tie each other up, she is the horse most likely to ruthlessly capitalise.

Musical Times is unbeaten but makes his debut on soft ground today; if he struggles for his usual fluent action early, William Buick may find the pace battle takes more out of him than in his two smooth good-ground wins.

Scommessa Sicura's repeated second-place finishes despite front-running suggest rivals consistently find more late — watch whether Oisin Murphy attempts to modify tactics given the crowded pace scenario, or commits to the lead regardless.

Eabha's twice-proven form on soft ground makes her the one prominently-ridden filly with a genuine going edge over most rivals — monitor how Charles Bishop positions her in relation to the front-running group in the first two furlongs.

runners_data.name: Waasil
