runners_data.comment: Waasil arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip, with a trainer firing at 30% over the past fortnight adding real confidence; the chief concern is whether 49 days off the track has left him short of a peak effort under 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Zarakova
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly improved sharply to win over a mile on Good at Nottingham last time and handles the trip well, but her style commits her to fighting for position against at least two other confirmed leaders — Oisin Murphy may be forced to concede the early battle or burn her out chasing it.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Zarakova looks hard to fancy despite a win last time out, with a sixth three starts back and the wide gap between her official mark of 82 and a speed rating of 68 suggesting she has plenty to find here.

runners_data.name: Metamouse
runners_data.note: Has solid form on soft and Good-to-Soft ground — winning at 6f on Soft and placed on similar going — giving her a genuine going advantage over most rivals; Laura Pearson's 0/20 14-day trainer stat is a flag, and the step to a mile from 7f needs accepting, but her prominent style suits the expected scenario.
runners_data.comment: Metamouse shaped well when third last time out and is a winner three starts back, his 123 lb burden and a trainer in a cold spell of 0/20 over 14 days the chief concerns, though he has distance and going experience and our rating of 88 marks him as a live threat.

runners_data.name: Keep Grating
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 7f on Good at Newmarket but has been improving steadily; Richard Hannon's juvenile is one of three horses all wanting the same piece of real estate at the first bend, which makes his task harder regardless of ability — most likely to be the one squeezed out of the lead battle by classier rivals.
runners_data.comment: Keep Grating won last time out and was third three starts back, which shows some ability, but a struggling trainer (2/53 in the last 14 days) and ranking fifth of six on our figures make him hard to fancy at face value.

runners_data.name: Primal
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani's mount carries Andrew Balding's second string and a form string of 64842 that suggests inconsistency; a natural prominent-style racer shown at the back of this mapping because the field lacks true hold-up horses, so its effectiveness from a patient position is discounted — the STYLE_FIT of 0.80 reflects that this is not its natural way of racing.
runners_data.comment: Primal has run over today's trip and returns just 15 days since his last outing, that runner-up finish last time out the most encouraging piece of recent form for a colt our rating marks as 5lb ahead of his official figure; the risk is he remains winless in his last five starts.

races.paceDynamic: Waasil, Zarakova, and Keep Grating are all confirmed front-runners over a flat Doncaster mile on Good To Soft ground, making a contested, honest gallop from the outset almost inevitable — three two-year-olds fighting for the lead across the opening furlongs will burn energy early and test stamina reserves significantly. The pace war will stretch the field out through the long Doncaster straight, creating a high-tempo scenario where those who try to lead from the front risk tying up in the ground before the finish. Al Wathba and Metamouse, racing prominently off a honest pace rather than setting it, are best positioned to capitalise as the front-runners exhaust each other, while Primal — a natural prominent runner redistributed to a notional hold-up role in a field light on true closers — offers less certainty from the back. This race shape emphatically favours prominent hold-up types who can sit just off the pace war, conserve energy through the middle stages, and pounce in the final two furlongs; pure speed-from-the-front profiles are compromised by the multi-horse pace contest. The field contains more front-running types than the race can accommodate cleanly at the head, with Waasil holding the most tactical authority to secure the rail given his recent winning form and Sam James's positional awareness, while Zarakova and Keep Grating are most likely to be nudged into a pace-pressing contest they cannot fully control.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Waasil, Zarakova, and Keep Grating all contest the early lead at a sapping gallop on soft ground, draining their reserves.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners trade head-to-head fractions through the first half-mile, leaving them vulnerable in the straight as the ground bites; the race becomes a stamina test decided late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Waasil Controls And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Waasil asserts cleanly from the break, gets a soft lead, and dictates a rhythm that suits his stamina profile.
scenarios.body: Sam James finds a sensible front position and Waasil, who has won at this trip on Good ground, converts his lead-from-the-front form — the rivals fail to coordinate a threat from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely contested but settles slightly, allowing a prominent racer to travel sweetly and pounce.
scenarios.body: Al Wathba, prominent off William Buick's positive ride, tracks the pace battle and finds more late than the leaders — his Stamina-ground form and OR advantage over the field makes him the logical beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses the field entirely and Primal, tracking from the rear despite not being a natural hold-up type, catches the carnage.
scenarios.body: Primal's redistribution to a hold-up role is artificial — this shape depends on a horse racing out of character — and the modest OR of 76 further limits ceiling, but a true stamina meltdown could bring it into play.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Waasil vs Zarakova vs Keep Grating at the break — if all three push hard for the lead over the first furlong, the pace could become genuinely destructive on soft ground, dramatically inflating the chances of Al Wathba and Metamouse.

Zarakova's jockey Oisin Murphy may attempt to bully the lead position given her recent winning confidence, but doing so against two equally committed front-runners risks burning her stamina before the straight — monitor her early positioning closely.

Metamouse's trainer David Loughnane has zero winners from 20 runners in the past 14 days — in a race where her prominent style genuinely suits the shape, that form concern at stable level is worth factoring before committing to her.

Al Wathba is 15 days since his last run and William Buick takes the ride — Charlie Appleby's runners with Buick up after a short break from a positive recent form string often arrive cherry-ripe, and the OR of 91 makes him the class benchmark in this field.

Keep Grating drops to OR 77 having improved through the season but faces the toughest positional challenge of any runner here — if he fails to secure a lead role early, his form profile suggests he lacks the gears to win from a chasing position on soft ground.

races.name: East Midlands Airport And JET2 Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Kach Above
runners_data.note: Two wins on the bounce over this exact course and distance on good ground, and a confirmed front-runner who commands the field on form — soft going is an unknown risk versus previous quick-ground wins, and at 135lbs she carries a notable weight burden after a 48-day absence.

runners_data.name: Undiscovered
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly arrives with an excellent trainer 14-day strike rate of 9/48 and a convincing soft-ground win on her form profile, making the step into this competitive handicap on good-to-soft a well-timed move with Rossa Ryan a significant booking.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins two and three starts back make Undiscovered the one to beat here, and he has run over today's trip before; the 44-day break is the only question mark, though his profile under top weight of 134 lb from stall one still reads like a winner's.

runners_data.name: Rafe's Da Man
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's colt won last time over this exact trip on good ground and Ryan Moore's presence elevates his market position considerably; his recent form string shows gradual improvement but all four runs have come on good, so good-to-soft is a slight query.
runners_data.comment: Rafe's Da Man appeals strongly on the back of his latest win, and he has experience over today's trip to call on, but a trainer firing at just four per cent in the last fortnight is the significant concern.

runners_data.name: Weekend Roar
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's juvenile has winning form over six furlongs on good ground but placed a distant 15th on soft last time — that soft-ground run is a genuine concern given today's conditions, even with James Doyle aboard and a moderate weight of 127lbs.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back and third four starts back, Weekend Roar arrives here on the back of an unplaced effort last time out and faces a stiff ask carrying 127 lb from stall four, though he has run over today's trip and going and is fit enough at 21 days since his last run.

runners_data.name: Fuel The Jet
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner who won over this trip at seven furlongs on good ground but finished ninth on his most recent start; Tom Clover's improving 14-day figures (4/15) keep him relevant, though his tendency to press the pace in a strong-gallop scenario makes him vulnerable in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win two starts back before a disappointing ninth last time, and with today's trip already familiar, Fuel The Jet arrives fresh on 22 days' rest carrying 125 lb — the main risk is reproducing that latest below-par effort.

runners_data.name: Midgham Man
runners_data.note: Won over seven furlongs on soft ground 12 days ago — his soft-ground form is directly relevant today and he is the freshest of the front-runners; Lewis Edmunds has been booked for a horse in form, and the quick turnaround for Rod Millman's yard suggests confidence.
runners_data.comment: Midgham Man arrives on the back of a win last time out, is experienced over today's trip and conditions, and carries 124 lb from stall two — the main risk is whether that burden blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Storm Blade
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's mount has shown solid placed form at seven furlongs on good ground and holds solid Andrew Balding form credentials; his natural running style sits closer to midfield than true hold-up, so he will need to be ridden patiently against his instincts if he is to benefit from a pace meltdown.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Storm Blade faces a stiff task from stall 8 carrying 122 lb; a runner-up finish last time out and experience over today's trip are the modest positives to set against a 47-day absence.

runners_data.name: Love Rome
runners_data.note: Placed in three consecutive seven-furlong races at this course and distance, which is compelling course form; the headgear flag is notable and she is inclined to press the pace, meaning she risks getting caught in the front-running war without the rating to overpower rivals on the line.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in his last three starts, Love Rome brings a string of placed efforts to the table, and has run over today's trip; the 32-day break and a solid rating of 87 offer encouragement, though converting that form into a win remains the challenge.

runners_data.name: Sanbona Warrior
runners_data.note: Won at seven furlongs on good ground and placed on a similar stamina-sapping surface, giving him relevant form credentials; William Knight's yard has been active (5/14 at 14 days) and Marco Ghiani's booking on a 77-rated horse looks like a live each-way claim if the pace scenario plays out as expected.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Sanbona Warrior faces a stiff ask, and a speed rating of 69 does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's trip and a win two starts back shows he can find the winning post.

races.paceDynamic: Kach Above, Fuel The Jet, and Midgham Man are all confirmed front-runners in a field of nine, with Love Rome also inclined to press the pace, guaranteeing a genuinely strong gallop from the outset on good-to-soft ground at Doncaster's flat, unrelenting seven furlongs. That pace congestion from four horses scrambling for the lead creates significant early pressure, and on a softening surface that will stretch stamina, any runner who burns energy fighting for position in the first two furlongs will pay for it in the closing stages. Storm Blade, the sole runner with a redistributed midfield-to-hold-up tag, is in truth not a natural closer, meaning the field offers very little genuine late cover from behind the pace. This race shape strongly favours stalking types or hold-up runners with proven stamina — specifically those who can sit just off the scorching early pace and pick up the pieces when the front-runners collide and tie up. The field holds more front-running or prominent types than can realistically secure their position; of those, Kach Above and Midgham Man, both winners at seven furlongs on similar going, are best-placed to actually control or dictate from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the multi-runner speed duel causes the front trio to set a ruinous gallop, the prominent stalkers absorb the pace and overhaul them late.
scenarios.body: Kach Above, Fuel The Jet, and Midgham Man cut each other's throats through the first three furlongs on softening ground, leaving Undiscovered, Rafe's Da Man, and Sanbona Warrior, who travel just off the pace, to mow them down in the final two furlongs where stamina dominates. Good-to-soft conditions amplify the damage of a hot early pace, rewarding anything that conserves energy through the mid-race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Kach Above or Midgham Man establishes a comfortable lead without serious early competition, dictating an honest but not punishing gallop.
scenarios.body: With rivals like Fuel The Jet failing to match the pace or backing off early, the front-runner settles into a rhythm that is sustainable on the flat Doncaster straight, building a lead that proves too big to close on ground that does not accelerate well. Kach Above, with two consecutive seven-furlong wins at Doncaster on good ground and strong form, is the most likely candidate to steal a march if rivals blink.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Powerfully
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses spectacularly in the final quarter mile, allowing the deepest-sitting runners to run through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: Storm Blade, redistributed from midfield but holding the most prominent rear position, and Love Rome, who has finished second twice at seven furlongs on this course, can still benefit if the front group implodes fully and there is genuine daylight through which to run. Doncaster's straight layout offers no hiding place for tired leaders, so a truly burned-up pace scenario can create a long flat run-in that suits residual stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not ruinous, compressing the field into a tight finish with multiple horses in contention entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Soft ground and a competitive but measured gallop create a scenario where several horses hit the line together, rewarding the horse who benefits most from Ryan Moore's tactical intelligence aboard Rafe's Da Man or Rossa Ryan's experience on Undiscovered. In a compressed finish at this level a one-pound weight advantage or a well-timed challenge becomes decisive, with the higher-rated horses likely shading the verdict.

watchPoints.text: Kach Above and Midgham Man — both confirmed front-runners who will inevitably clash for the early lead, and whichever one blinks first could compromise the chance of both by burning excessive early energy on soft ground.

Fuel The Jet — finished ninth last time out after winning over this trip, and a repeat of a strong early pace challenge could see him fold badly in the straight, opening the door for stalkers behind him.

Weekend Roar — his soft-ground form (15th on his most recent soft run) stands out sharply in a race where conditions are likely to emphasise stamina; James Doyle cannot compensate for a horse with a known soft-ground question mark.

Storm Blade — watch where Oisin Murphy positions him at the start; if Murphy commits to tracking the pace rather than settling deep, the redistributed hold-up tag becomes academic and he morphs into a legitimate pace-stalker threat for Andrew Balding.

Sanbona Warrior — low-rated at 77 but with proven soft-ground placed form and a yard in good recent form; if the pace scenario unfolds as projected, watch for Ghiani to angle him widest of all to find clear running in the straight.

races.name: Pertemps Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Mocking
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse for Murtagh who has won and placed in similar going, but absent 80 days and carrying a hood; redistributed into the pace map's midfield zone as there are too many genuine closers for all to race at the rear — its chance is best served if the pace truly collapses.|
runners_data.comment: Mocking showed he can win in recent starts but has disappointed in his last three outings, and an 80-day absence adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going before, and carries 133 lb off an official mark of 79.

runners_data.name: Devil's Peak
runners_data.note: Buick takes the ride for Gosden on this three-year-old who placed at 2/11f on Good ground; a genuine hold-up horse but jockey class and a wide-margin win at 1m1f suggest he can be positioned cleverly — best chance arrives if the race develops into a sprint finish from midfield.|
runners_data.comment: Devil's Peak landed the spoils three starts back and arrives with a trainer firing at 37% over the past fortnight, giving him every chance off 132 lb; the main concern is that he finished sixth last time out.

runners_data.name: Railwayview Lady
runners_data.note: Cromwell's four-year-old has failed to trouble the judge in five of her last six on comparable going and her recent form string of 20-889 does not inspire; a natural hold-up type shuffled into midfield on the map, she faces a stiff task converting from a position that does not suit her.|
runners_data.comment: Railwayview Lady showed a second in her recent form and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her more than a live threat at a mark of 78; however, the trainer is yet to land a winner in the last 14 days (0 from 39), and four consecutive unplaced efforts since that placing are the key concern.

runners_data.name: Masterinthewoods
runners_data.note: Lavelle's four-year-old has been a model of consistency, placing in four consecutive races at 1m2f on Good ground; Probert is a capable handler and the horse's willingness to grind suggests Good to Soft and a stamina test at 1m4f could bring out further improvement, racing from a hold-up base.|
runners_data.comment: Masterinthewoods has been a model of consistency, placing second in three successive starts and winning four runs back, and 26 days between runs leaves him fresh for this test; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 136 lb is within range for a gelding rated 82 officially.

runners_data.name: My Ballyquinn
runners_data.note: Tudhope's three-year-old has won twice at 1m4f on Good and placed twice more at the trip, making it the most course-and-distance-relevant hold-up horse in the race; 19 days since last run is fine, and a recent 12th in soft gives mild ground concern, though it has the tactical profile to stalk and strike.|
runners_data.comment: My Ballyquinn arrives on the back of a lively recent sequence — two wins and two seconds in his last six starts — and has experience of today's trip and conditions; at 135 lb, the weight he carries is the one factor to keep onside.

runners_data.name: Alfred Wincham
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, he set his own pace to win over 1m2f on Good and will be unopposed at the head of affairs; the [STYLE_FIT] flag reflects that a truly strong pace-pressing field could expose him, but with no rival to pressurise him this is a significant advantage on the flat Doncaster track.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of our figures and 8lb below the official rating, Alfred Wincham looks hard to fancy here, though a win one start back offers some encouragement and he has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Mr Freedom
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with experience over big-field staying trips, including a win at 1m4f on Good; a prominent racer who will likely slot in behind Alfred Wincham and keep the pace honest without forcing a genuine breakneck gallop — going and trip suit, though his OR of 77 makes him vulnerable to classier rivals late.|
runners_data.comment: Mr Freedom is yet to win in his last five starts, though a third three starts back offers some encouragement; returning after 71 days off and carrying 131 lb, the step up in weight looks the main obstacle for this mid-ranking contender.

runners_data.name: Eniac
runners_data.note: Moore's booking is significant for this Brian Ellison three-year-old, who has placed three times in his last six including at Doncaster's straight mile; a true hold-up type whose instinct is to come from behind, mapped to midfield because the race shape is loaded with closers — Moore's positional awareness is his biggest asset here.|

runners_data.name: Brighton View
runners_data.note: A progressive three-year-old for William Knight who has won at 1m2f on Good and placed at the same trip; his natural hold-up style means he has been placed into the midfield zone on the map, and with five wins or places in his last five runs he has form, though the step up to 1m4f on Good to Soft is a new question.|
runners_data.comment: Brighton View sits well below the top-rated runners on our figures and must find significant improvement to threaten, though he does bring distance and going experience, arrives placed last time out, and the 33-day break leaves him reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Itica
runners_data.note: Balding's three-year-old won last time at 1m1f on Soft for Murphy, which is an encouraging combination of jockey, trainer strike rate and going; racing from a prominent position, she steps up sharply in trip to 1m4f and it remains uncertain whether she truly stays — the going is fine but stamina is unproven.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten in three of his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Itica is hard to fancy despite a win last time out; he has run over today's trip and returns after just 11 days, but the ratings profile makes him a tough sell.

races.paceDynamic: Alfred Wincham is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine rival to challenge him for the lead, he will set a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Soft ground over 1m4f at Doncaster's flat, straight track. Mr Freedom and Itica are the only other horses with prominent tendencies and may track Alfred Wincham closely, but neither is likely to pressurise him into a genuinely strong pace, meaning the race will likely be run at a measured tempo that rewards those who can travel into the race and produce a sustained finish rather than a sprint. The bulk of the field — Mocking, Devil's Peak, Railwayview Lady, Masterinthewoods, My Ballyquinn, Eniac, and Brighton View — are natural hold-up types, but the field holds more genuine closers than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, so several of these will be pushed forward into midfield against their instincts, with Devil's Peak and My Ballyquinn the most likely to secure a comfortable stalking position given jockey class and recent experience at this trip. This race shape — a steady lead, a bunched midfield, and a sprint-style finish — strongly favours those able to race prominently or within easy striking distance of the pace, as true hold-up horses will be covering extra ground late on ground that will blunt a finishing burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Alfred Wincham dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the closers are unable to muster sufficient momentum on Good to Soft ground in the straight.
scenarios.body: Alfred Wincham sets a sedate fractions-based tempo that saps the finishing kick of the hold-up horses strung out behind him, and he or a prominent tracker collects as the late runners fail to close the gap in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalker Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent tracker — racing in a natural stalking position just off Alfred Wincham — produces a clean, sustained run through the final two furlongs on the flat Doncaster straight.
scenarios.body: My Ballyquinn or Masterinthewoods, positioned within two lengths of the pace, kicks past Alfred Wincham in the final furlong having been delivered with a well-timed run; this scenario suits horses proven at this trip who can travel prominently.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and the field bunches, creating a genuine sprint finish that allows a horse launching from midfield to pick through.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up horse redistributed into midfield — most likely Devil's Peak or Eniac with top-level jockey craft from Buick or Moore — finds a clear run and runs on powerfully through the final furlong on ground they handle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Alfred Wincham goes off too fast for the conditions and fades badly, causing a dramatic reshuffle that drags the race into a test of stamina and resolution.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses given too much to do early would need the front end to come back to them in the final half-mile, a scenario that is unlikely given Alfred Wincham's profile and the steady gallop expected.

watchPoints.text: Alfred Wincham is entirely unopposed for the lead — if Rossa Ryan elects to dawdle in front, the entire field could be caught flat-footed with a field of hold-up horses unable to close from too far back in the straight.

My Ballyquinn and Devil's Peak both have top jockeys who will be fighting for the same stalking position just off the pace — watch how Tudhope and Buick position early, as a congestion incident in the back straight could compromise multiple fancied runners.

Eniac and Brighton View are genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield by the race shape — Ryan Moore on Eniac in particular may attempt to find a position closer than expected, creating a pocket situation if the pace is slow and the field remains tightly bunched turning for home.

The going for this race is officially Good to Soft (the Soft designation in the race header appears to conflict with the on-the-day going report, which reads Good to Soft throughout the card) — horses with soft-ground form flags should not be unduly penalised, but the track is unlikely to be as testing as a true Soft surface.
